How is the AI-driven memory shortage inflating the price of consumer electronics? Asset and Wealth Management’s Michael Cembalest weighs in on China’s imbalanced economy and unrelenting mercantilism in the latest Eye on the Market. How are global and regional ETF markets performing?        Discover how the rise of real-time payments is reshaping cash flow for businesses.  Want more content from In Context? Sign up here to receive weekly insights directly in your inbox. The AI infrastructure buildout is fueling “chipflation” AI data center demand is creating a shortage of global memory capacity, with prices for dynamic random access memory (DRAM) estimated to rise more than 400% from the start of 2024 to the end of 2026, according to J.P. Morgan Global Research. For the average consumer, implications of the memory shortage may already be felt in the form of “chipflation,” or inflation of the cost of memory for chips in common electronics — from phones and computers to smartwatches and TVs. In many cases, manufacturers pass through these elevated costs in the form of raised prices. At what cost? 🔗 Eye on the Market: The Year of the Trojan Fire Horse China is living up to the anthropomorphic characteristics of this year’s zodiac, the Fire Horse, in at least one regard: bold moves, self-reliance, speed, action and innovation when it comes to the energy transition. On the other hand, like the Trojan horse in “The Odyssey,” the gift of inexpensive Chinese exports is not always as beneficial as it seems. Read the report 🔗 By the numbers 400%   Prices for dynamic random access memory (DRAM) are projected to climb >400% from the start of 2024 to the end of 2026. 23% The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for software and accessories and Producer Price Index (PPI) for storage devices have both risen by 23% since the end of 2024. $500B  The global real-time payments market is expected to grow from $34 billion in 2025 to nearly $500 billion by 2034. Understanding the $22 trillion ETF industry ETFs continue to grow in scale and complexity, with total assets under management up 43% year over year as of April 2026. In particular, active ETFs remain a key focus for both issuers and investors across the globe. 77592.subject: Hyperliquid’s Spot Wars
77592.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

BTC continues to struggle while gold regains momentum. Bitcoin fell 3.1% last week even as equities and gold moved higher, with softer inflation data reducing expectations for another Fed hike. 

Meanwhile, Hyperliquid has found its next battleground. After HIP-3 drove its expansion into RWA perps, xStocks, EQX and Dinari are now competing to build out tokenized equities on spot. We look at whether the market can finally gain traction, alongside compute futures and tokenization’s shift from access to utility.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

BTC once again looked weak last week, falling 3.1% while every other major benchmark ended higher. The Nasdaq led with a 1.4% gain, followed by gold at 0.8% and the S&P 500 at 0.5%.

Gold had a stellar start to the year, with YTD gains peaking at 30% toward the end of January. It then spent much of the year giving those returns back, falling from around $5.6K per ounce to $4K. Over the past month, however, gold has started to look strong again, gaining 10.7% and comfortably outperforming the other major benchmarks.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/38fda02b-b76d-4895-8218-3d46d85cd453/image.png?t=1786967450)
Caption: 

Softer inflation data last week [reduced](https://www.reuters.com/business/gold-gains-weaker-dollar-reduced-fed-rate-hike-bets-2026-08-17/) expectations that the Fed will raise interest rates next month, with the odds falling from 47% a month ago to 30% today. At the same time, central banks have continued to buy gold at record levels. According to the World Gold Council, net purchases between April and June were more than [five](https://www.reuters.com/commentary/reuters-open-interest/central-banks-spearhead-renewed-gold-rush-2026-08-13/) times higher than during the previous three months.

While gold and BTC are both seen as hedges against inflation and dollar debasement, the same momentum has yet to reach Bitcoin. BTC remains stuck between $62K and $64K, while weekly ETF flows continue to flip between inflows and outflows. Funds recorded $159M of net outflows last week.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f4537cce-a403-4f43-96ee-cf6a902e10c4/image.png?t=1786967449)
Caption: 

Across the different sectors, the Oracle index led the market with a 14.5% gain, followed by L2s at 6.7%.

77591.subject: 🔑 How Claude's text watermark works
77591.body:
The Atlas

Автор: GenAI Works


Автор: GenAI Works

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/how-claudes-text-watermark-works-genai-works-i1v1f?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BJA7PmdJyQ4eRAbcSmxBDnw%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2hXFn411yhsYo1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~msxarfeq~ls-null-null&eid=fz96fz-msxarfeq-ls
  
Welcome back! Today: the mechanism behind Claude's watermark, the tool built to strip it, GitHub's fix for vibe coding and NVIDIA teaching models to share memory. In today's Atlas Newsletter: What does the watermark actually change? Nothing gets inserted into your text, and the randomness behind every word choice comes from a key instead. Can you remove it? A Skill shipped in under 24 hours to strip marks from Claude, Gemini and OpenAI, and its own repo argues against using half of it. Still prompting and praying? GitHub's Spec Kit makes the agent write an executable specification before it touches a line of code. Why does switching models cost you twice? NVIDIA found the relationship between two models' KV caches is linear enough to map with ridge regression and skip prefill entirely. PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Anthropic shares more details about how Claude’s new watermarks will work Anthropic published a detailed explainer on how its text watermarking works.  Nothing gets inserted, no hidden characters, no extra tokens, no change in price or speed. Here's the mechanism.  A model picks one token at a time from a list of candidates.  In "The weather today was cold and…" the next word is likely "overcast" or "grey," and which one rarely matters to the meaning, so a random number settles it.  Watermarking changes where that randomness comes from.  The model uses a key plus the preceding words to decide, and anyone holding the key can check whether a sequence matches what Claude would have produced with it. The method is a version of SynthID-Text, published by Google DeepMind in Nature in 2024.  DeepMind tested for quality impact across live Gemini traffic and found no statistically significant difference. The limitations are the useful part. The watermark lives only in low-stakes choices, so it thins wherever precision is required.  After "Isaac Newton's most famous work was called Principia," there's one correct next word and nothing to work with. Same for code. Short passages offer too few choices to reach confidence. Proofreading barely marks at all, since almost every word stays the human's. Anthropic states the limit plainly: a watermark shows Claude was likely involved, and cannot separate "Claude wrote this" from "Claude heavily edited
